display.title: The Rebbe, Our Shepherd
display.summary_short: The Tzemach Tzedek sends a trembling Chassid to tell a cruel poritz it is time to do teshuvah, then explains with a shepherd's parable why some sheep must be carried out of the pit.
display.summary_long: After the song 'I Believe in Hashem', the storyteller tells a story passed down by a great-nephew of the Tzemach Tzedek. Reb Dov, a Chassid from Romania, travels some 800 miles by horse and wagon to the Rebbe and back. On the way home he stops for Shabbos in a city where a very old Chassid, who knew the Mitteler Rebbe and perhaps the Alter Rebbe, speaks only at Shalosh Seudos. Reb Dov cannot hear the story over the crowd, so the old rav repeats it for him. Once the Tzemach Tzedek sent a Chassid to a Jew-hating poritz guarded by vicious dogs and armed men, with one message: it is time for you to do teshuvah. Protected by a holy Name of Hashem the Rebbe taught him, the Chassid walked in unharmed, delivered the words and left, and then forgot the Name. The poritz vanished, and months later a silent beggar sat in the Lubavitch shul, crying over Tehillim and fasting. When the Chassidim asked why the poritz got such a shortcut while they must work all their lives, the Tzemach Tzedek answered with the parable of a shepherd who calls stray sheep back but must climb down and carry one that has fallen into a pit.
display.lesson: The Rebbe is a shepherd who cares for every Jew; most of us can return to the path when called, and no Jew is ever too far to come back.

advisories.note: A Chassid walks past vicious dogs and armed guards to an evil poritz; he is unharmed.
The poritz is known as a Jew-hater who caused the Jews much trouble.
